evidence.claim: Madison’s green began as the site of the East Guilford parish meetinghouse in 1705; the village center became a town center when Madison incorporated in 1826.
evidence.quote: The green was established in 1705, when the area became the site of a meeting house for the newly authorized East Guilford parish (the area then being part of Guilford).  From this beginning it grew as a village center, which became the town center when Madison was incorporated in 1826.

evidence.claim: Samson Rock is a glacial erratic boulder set between two shopping centers and a parking lot.
evidence.quote: Samson or Sampson's Rock is a glacial erratic boulder in Madison in New Haven County, Connecticut.

evidence.claim: A somewhat foot-shaped indentation marks its top.
evidence.quote: The rock contains a somewhat foot-shaped indent on top

evidence.claim: In Algonquin legend, the giant Odziozo dropped the rock while throwing earth into the sea to form Tuxis Island, then stepped on it as he left.
evidence.quote: According to Algonquin legend, the rock was formed by Odziozo, a giant and folk hero. The legend says Odziozo created it after he flung some land out to sea, creating Tuxis Island. The hole filled up to become Tuxis Pond. One rock fell from his hand and became Samson Rock. While leaving, he stepped on the rock.

evidence.claim: European settlers recast the figure as the biblical Samson, giving the boulder its name.
evidence.quote: The European settlers assigned this legend to the Biblical Samson after being told the legend in the 1600s, giving the rock its  name.
